title: What Happens When an AI Agent Reads Every Email in a Claims Inbox
summary: How an AI agent reads every email in a quality claims inbox, logs each claim with its evidence, and sorts out the rest.
body_markdown:
An AI agent can read every email that lands in a quality claims inbox, separate the new claims from the replies, reminders and unrelated mail, and log each claim in a register with the depot, the delivery, the product, the quantity, the reason and links to the evidence. Our claims agent at a fresh-produce multinational has read more than 7,000 emails so far and logged 1,700 quality claims from depots in 17 European countries.


## TL;DR


- A claims inbox mixes new claims with follow-ups, credit-note threads, delivery questions and noise, in several languages.
- The agent reads all of it, logs each new claim as one structured record, and links follow-ups to the claim they belong to.
- It records what the customer reported and keeps the photos and documents as evidence. The quality team still decides each claim.
- You end up with a complete register, including the claims nobody had time to log in a busy week.


## What does a quality claims inbox look like before an agent?


For a supplier of fresh goods, a claims inbox is where receiving depots report what went wrong with a delivery: bruised fruit, wrong ripeness, short quantities, damaged pallets. The reports arrive from many countries and in several languages. Some are a single line with a photo. Some are a filled-in form as a PDF. Many are replies to an earlier thread, adding a photo or asking where the credit note is.


Somebody on the quality team reads each one, works out whether it is a new claim, finds the delivery it refers to, and types the details into a register or a spreadsheet. That is manageable in a quiet week, but in a heatwave, when claims spike across every depot at once, the backlog grows exactly when the business most needs to see the pattern.


## What does the claims agent do with each email?


1. **Reads the whole message** , including forwarded mail and attachments, in the language it was written in.
2. **Decides what it is** : a new claim, a follow-up to an existing claim, or something else, such as a delivery query or an internal note.
3. **Extracts the claim facts** : the depot, the delivery date, the order or delivery reference, the product, the affected quantity and the reason the customer gave.
4. **Normalises them** : depot names and country spellings mapped to one list, quantities to one unit, the reason to the categories the quality team uses.
5. **Logs one record per claim** in the claims register, with links to the original email and the attached photos and documents.
6. **Links follow-ups** to the claim they belong to, so a reminder does not become a second claim.


## Why does reading every email matter?


When every claim from every depot sits in one register with the same fields, the quality team can see which product, which supplier or which route is causing trouble this week, and act on it the same week.


It also changes the conversation with customers. When a depot asks about a claim, the team finds it in seconds, with the original email one click away.


## What does the agent leave to the quality team?


The decision. Whether a claim is accepted, whether it is credited and for how much, and whether a supplier is charged back are judgement calls with commercial weight. The agent prepares a complete record for each one, and the quality team decides.


One limit is deliberate: the agent keeps photos attached as evidence and does not grade produce quality from a phone picture. It takes the claim reason from what the customer wrote, and grading ripeness from an image stays with the quality team.


## How does IT stay in control?


IT approves read access to the claims mailbox and write access to the claims register, once. The agent can do nothing outside those connections. Every record links back to the email it came from, and every run is logged, so a disputed claim can be traced to its source. More on that model in[what an AI agent audit trail needs](https://clarm.com/blog/articles/ai-agent-audit-trail) .


## How do you start with your own claims inbox?


1. Export a few weeks of real claims mail, including the replies and the noise.
2. Write down the fields your register needs and the reason categories your team uses.
3. Collect the reference lists: depots, customers, products.
4. Run the agent on that history and compare its register with what the team logged by hand, claim by claim.


If the comparison finds claims the team never logged, report that number first.


## FAQ


### Can an AI agent process quality claims from a shared inbox?


Yes. The agent reads every incoming email, decides whether it is a new claim, and logs each claim in a register with the depot, the delivery, the product, the quantity, the reason and links to the evidence. At a fresh-produce multinational, our claims agent has read 7,000+ emails and logged 1,700 quality claims from depots in 17 European countries.


### Does the agent decide whether a claim is justified?


No. It records the facts the customer reported and attaches the evidence. The decision to accept, reject or credit a claim stays with the quality team, which now starts from a complete, structured record.


### Can the agent judge produce quality from photos?


We do not claim that. The agent keeps the photos attached to the claim as evidence for the quality team. Grading fruit from a phone photo is outside what the agent does.


### What happens to emails that are not claims?


The agent sorts them: reminders and replies are linked to the claim they belong to, and delivery queries, credit notes and other mail are marked as not a claim, so nothing in the inbox goes unread.
